title: shortcuts with pressed Alt don't work when keymap is changed
author: mozdzierz
summary: Right-Alt text remaps stop applying after changing between Japanese IME and Polish/US layouts, but current behavior and the role of IME versus AltGr are not established.

confidence.rationale: The requested reproduction matrix directly separates the two likely mechanisms.

judgment.rationale: The report has useful steps, yet it predates current Keyboard Manager behavior and does not show whether the failure occurs without IME or which exact layout transition changes AltGr state.
evidence: Right Alt+A/C are mapped to Polish characters and work until the input layout changes.
After switching layouts while holding Right Alt, only the first remapped character is emitted.
The latest comment asks for a current retest and a no-IME comparison; no answer is present.
judgment.recommended_action: Request the exact current layout transition and a no-IME comparison before selecting AltGr or IME state handling.

fix_assessment.rationale: The current report does not yet distinguish an IME-specific interaction from general AltGr/modifier-state handling.

issue_context.summary: Right-Alt text remaps stop applying after changing between Japanese IME and Polish/US layouts, but current behavior and the role of IME versus AltGr are not established.
known_information: Japanese IME, Polish (Programmers), and US International layouts are involved.
The failure depends on holding Right Alt continuously across multiple action keys.
inferences: The layout switch may change Right Alt interpretation between a standalone modifier and AltGr (Ctrl+Alt), leaving Keyboard Manager's pressed-key state inconsistent.
issue_context.analysis: The plausible AltGr-state hypothesis is useful but not yet enough for a fix. A bounded current reproduction matrix can identify whether IME, layout change, or continuous modifier state is necessary.
initial_investigation: Read the complete report, both comments, labels, and linked similar issues.
Separated continuous Right Alt handling from the act of switching input layouts.

information_gaps.information: Whether the issue persists on the current stable PowerToys release.
information_gaps.why_needed: Determines whether later AltGr fixes changed the behavior.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Retest and provide the About version.

information_gaps.information: The starting and destination layouts, input method, and exact Right-Alt mappings.
information_gaps.why_needed: Determines when Right Alt is interpreted as AltGr and which transition corrupts state.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: List the layouts in Windows order and each mapping exactly as displayed in Keyboard Manager.

information_gaps.information: Whether the failure reproduces without Japanese IME and whether releasing Right Alt after the layout switch resets it.
information_gaps.why_needed: Separates IME interaction from a general held-modifier state bug.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Repeat the numbered sequence once with only Polish/US layouts and report whether releasing Right Alt restores subsequent remaps.

actions.label: Confirm the IME and AltGr transition

comment.body:
Thanks for documenting the held-Right-Alt sequence and the affected layouts. To distinguish an IME interaction from a general AltGr/modifier-state bug, please provide.

1. The current PowerToys version and whether the issue still reproduces.
2. The exact starting and destination keyboard layouts plus the mappings as shown in Keyboard Manager.
3. The same test without Japanese IME enabled.
4. Whether releasing and pressing Right Alt again immediately restores the remaps.

This matrix will identify whether the fix belongs in layout-change handling, AltGr state tracking, or IME integration.
